summary.text: A 45-year-old woman with hypertension, treated with medicine for two years, and two previous strokes treated with medical and physiotherapy treatment was admitted in July with flaccidity of the right upper and lower limbs and very challenging bed mobility. She had no sensory issues or deformities, was oriented, scored GCS 7, NIHSS 30 and mRS 5, had hampered bowel and bladder function and was on intermittent catheterization, with a Ryle’s tube for feeding.

MRI revealed an area of blood density attenuation with multiple air foci in the left gangliocapsular region, and CT showed intracranial hemorrhage with resolving hemorrhage and mass effect, a 9 mm midline shift toward the left, a corpus callosum lipoma and right-sided bony defects. Vital signs were temperature 95.5 °F, BP 130/79 mmHg, pulse 63 and respiration 20 per minute, and oxygen saturation 98%.

She underwent a decompressive craniotomy and, after 36 hours of ICU monitoring, was shifted to the surgery ward. A rehabilitation program was planned and treatment began after surgery. Phase I (day 1 to four weeks) used Rood’s facilitation, inhibitory techniques, passive movement of the right upper limb, bed mobility exercises and oral facial facilitation; Phase II (four to eight weeks) included PNF, breathing exercises and oral motor drills.

Pretreatment and posttreatment scores were NIHSS 30/42 and 12/42, mRS 5/6 and 1/6, FIM 70/126 and 95/126, Brunnstrom upper and lower limb stage 1 and stage 5, and voluntary control Grade 0 and Grade 2. The authors describe the interventions as very effective, with a good recovery rate that improved quality of life and strength.
